_comment: senechal's typed front doors: the machine-readable contract `notify-senechal` files against, published here and FETCHED at call time rather than hardcoded in the caller. WHY (2026-08-16): the front door took free text and produced a prose GitHub issue, while every consumer downstream (health/dead-config.sh, health/hosts-unregistered.sh) reads structure -- so every filing needed a human to translate prose into schema, and health/unabsorbed-notices.sh existed only to nag about the backlog of untranslated prose. The note already knows its type at the call site: remedies/window-spawn-desktop.sh files a footprint record flattened into a sentence, then re-parsed by a human days later. A door makes that round trip unnecessary. Ownership: realisateur owns THAT doors exist and how the command is distributed; senechal owns WHAT EACH DOOR REQUIRES, i.e. this file -- so senechal can add a door without an edit in realisateur's repo. That seam is not theoretical: notify-senechal's filing footer is a senechal contract hardcoded in realisateur, and dropping it took tools/issue-janitor.py BLIND for a day (senechal#221).
_transport_comment: The transport stays a GitHub issue, because the live config is ~/.config/senechal/senechal.json on one host and a caller on `monkey` has neither a clone nor write access -- that constraint is what put prose in an issue in the first place, and it has not changed. What changes is the LETTER, not the mail slot: a fenced ```senechal-door block carrying a validated object, which tools/absorb-notices.py applies to the live config unattended. Label `door` is how the absorber finds them; `idea` stays on for continuity with issue-janitor.py's gates.
_no_prose_door_comment: There is deliberately no free-text door. If no door fits what an agent needs to file, the fix is to ADD ONE -- a PR to this file plus its apply rule in tools/absorb-notices.py -- not to fall back to a paragraph. A prose fallback would always be the path of least resistance, and every filing would take it, which is exactly the state this replaces.

footprint.comment: Something a project installed on a host that outlives the session that installed it. Lands in estate.footprint, probed thereafter by health/dead-config.sh.

help.id: stable slug, unique in the registry, e.g. crt-whisper-server
help.target: kind-specific: unit name, port number, or absolute path
help.host: which device in estate.devices it is installed on
help.owner: the project that fixes problems with it -- not senechal
help.retire: the exact command that finishes removing it
help.notes: why it exists, and what its removal is waiting on

footprint-correction.comment: A field on a footprint row already in estate.footprint is WRONG, and here is the evidence -- the same gap device-correction closed for estate.devices, one registry over (hf7y/senechal#633). The footprint door is add-only ON PURPOSE, so a fact recorded once and later found wrong had nowhere to land: `retire: "no"` on a file whose reason has evaporated reads as an instruction to keep it, and health/dead-config.sh probing by `target` only confirms the path still exists, never whether the row's story about it still holds. `field` is limited to the describing fields (notes, status, retire) -- not id, kind, target, host or owner, which are identity and delegation and stay human-only. `was` must match what the registry says RIGHT NOW so a filing built against a stale read is refused, and the value it replaces is kept beside the row in `corrections`, with the evidence for the change. Lands in estate.footprint, the same list the footprint door writes.

help.id: the footprint row to correct -- it must already be in estate.footprint
help.field: notes | status | retire -- the only agent-amendable fields
help.was: the field's CURRENT value, quoted exactly; a mismatch is refused, not applied
help.now: the corrected value, whole -- it replaces `was`, so carry over what is still true
help.evidence: how it was verified: the command run, the log line, the date

crontab.comment: A crontab entry another project's own account added on a host, so the change is senechal-visible instead of arriving as a hand-filed prose issue (hf7y/senechal#362, the second time this exact filing had no typed door to land in). Lands in estate.crontab, a separate registry from estate.footprint because footprint's target is restricted to a unit name, port number or absolute path and cannot carry a schedule or a command line.

help.tag: the trailing `# <owner>:<mechanism>:TICK` comment identifying the line -- names a MECHANISM, not an account, so the same tag recurs on purpose whenever several accounts run it (e.g. scheduler-paced-runner on crt, abletim, apms); the (host, account, tag) triple is what senechal#428/#430 found actually unique
help.host: which device in estate.devices the crontab lives on
help.account: the UNIX account whose crontab this is -- not necessarily the same as owner
help.owner: the project that owns this cron entry and fixes problems with it -- not senechal
help.command: the command line, including any inline env vars
help.retire: the exact command that removes this line, e.g. crontab -l | grep -v '<tag>' | crontab -
help.notes: why it exists, where a backup of the prior crontab was made, and what it writes

crontab-correction.comment: A field on a crontab row already in estate.crontab is WRONG, and here is the evidence -- the same gap footprint-correction closed for estate.footprint, one registry over (hf7y/senechal#633). The crontab door is add-only ON PURPOSE, so a park/re-arm cycle that changes a registered row's disposition had nowhere to land except a REJECTED filing (measured: 2026-09-04's mass park of scheduler-paced-runner across monkey rejected the 3 accounts already registered live, while the other 8 landed fine as new rows). `field` is limited to the describing fields (schedule, command, status, retire, notes) -- not tag, host, account or owner, which are identity and delegation and stay human-only. `was` must match what the registry says RIGHT NOW so a filing built against a stale read is refused, and the value it replaces is kept beside the row in `corrections`, with the evidence for the change. The key is composite (host, account, tag), the same triple the crontab door itself dedupes on. Lands in estate.crontab, the same list the crontab door writes.

help.host: the crontab row's host -- part of the key, must already be in estate.crontab
help.account: the crontab row's account -- part of the key
help.tag: the crontab row's tag -- part of the key
help.field: schedule | command | status | retire | notes -- the only agent-amendable fields
help.was: the field's CURRENT value, quoted exactly; a mismatch is refused, not applied
help.now: the corrected value, whole -- it replaces `was`, so carry over what is still true
help.evidence: how it was verified: the command run, the log line, the date

verb.comment: A verb `installe` put on PATH, so an install lands in estate.verbs instead of failing UNDECLARED (hf7y/senechal#414: this door did not exist, so every `installe verb` call ever filed one). Lands in estate.verbs, a separate registry from estate.footprint because footprint's target is restricted to a unit name, port number or absolute path and cannot carry which project owns the verb or which build it is pinned to -- the facts worth registering, per #414.

help.name: the verb's bare name, as it lands on PATH
help.host: which device in estate.devices it is installed on
help.account: the UNIX account whose ~/.local/bin or /usr/local/bin holds it
help.project: the project that owns the verb and fixes problems with it -- not senechal
help.build: the build id the link is pinned to, e.g. 2026-08-24T033024Z
help.retire: the exact command that removes it: installe retire <name>

device.comment: A machine senechal did not know about. Lands in estate.devices, after which every health check covers it, because they read this list and never their own host list.

help.name: short hostname, e.g. monkey
help.addr: how to reach it: localhost, an ssh host, or a .local name
help.expect: always-on | intermittent -- what an unreachable probe means
help.owner: who fixes problems in that device's domain
help.notes: what it is for, and what runs on it

device-correction.comment: A field on a device already in estate.devices is WRONG, and here is the evidence. The device door is add-only ON PURPOSE -- a filing may not silently overwrite a row a human wrote -- so a fact recorded once and later found wrong had nowhere to land, and went on living in private agent memory nobody maintains. This amends ONE field of ONE registered device and cannot clobber blind: `field` is limited to the two describing fields (owner, addr, reach and expect are Zach's delegation and probe policy, not observations, and stay human-only), `was` must match what the registry says RIGHT NOW so a filing built against a stale read is refused rather than applied, and the value it replaces is kept beside the row in `corrections`, with the evidence for the change. Acceptance is the absorb PR, which was already a human's to merge (hf7y/senechal#411) -- deliberately no second queue to review. Lands in estate.devices, the same list the device door writes.

help.name: the device to correct -- it must already be in estate.devices
help.field: kind | notes -- the only agent-amendable fields
help.was: the field's CURRENT value, quoted exactly; a mismatch is refused, not applied
help.now: the corrected value, whole -- it replaces `was`, so carry over what is still true
help.evidence: how it was verified: the command run, the log line, the date

claude.comment: A deliberate change to the Claude harness under ~/.claude (settings, hooks, slash commands, memory) -- so the standing notify policy for that surface has somewhere to file, per hf7y/senechal#508. Lands in estate.claude_changes, one entry per filed change. Complementary to hf7y/senechal#460's canonical-content drift check, not a replacement: that remedy reports drift FROM canonical content; this door records a deliberate change someone made, and a change filed here should not later read as drift there. Not retirable like footprint/crontab/verb -- it is a record of an event, not a live installed thing, so there is no status/retire pair.

help.id: stable slug, unique in the registry, e.g. claude-config-memory-budget-trim-20260828
help.path: the changed file, relative to ~/.claude, e.g. projects/-home-zach.../memory/MEMORY.md
help.kind: settings | hooks | commands | memory -- which part of the harness this touches
help.host: which device in estate.devices the change was made on
help.owner: the project/agent that made the change -- not necessarily senechal
help.what: one line: what changed and why
